Person.comment:
Ron Caspi received his PhD in Marine Microbiology in 1996 from the Scripps Institution of Oceanography in La Jolla, CA, under the guidance of Dr. Bradley Tebo and Dr. Margo Haygood. He completed his post-graduate education in 1999 with Dr. Donald Helinski at the Center for Molecular Genetics at UC San Diego.

After three years with Pangene Corporation, where he managed the automation and bioinformatics department, Ron joined SRI International in 2004, and has been the head curator of the MetaCyc database ever since.

Protein.comment:
Methanogenesis from H2, CO2, or acetate is dependent on the presence of sodium ions. The sodium ion-dependent step has been shown to be the transfer of a methyl group from N5-methyltetrahydromethanopterin to coenzyme M. The exergonic methyl transfer reaction is coupled to the endergonic pumping of sodium ions out of the cell, forming an ion gradient across the membrane. The two processes are catalyzed by a membrane-associated Na+-translocating/methyltranferase multienzyme complex composed of eight different subunits, MtrA-H. In methanogens lacking cytochromes, the MtrA-H reaction represents the only chemiosmotic process [Gottschalk01].

Primary structure analysis predicts MtrC, MtrD and MtrE as integral membrane proteins with at least six transmembrane helices, MtrA, MtrB, MtrF and MtrG as peripheral proteins with one transmembrane helix anchor, and MtrH as a peripheral protein without a membrane anchor. The only prosthetic group is Coα-[α-(5-hydroxybenzimidazolyl)]-cob(I)amide, which is is axially coordinated by a histidine residue of the MtrA subunit (His84 in Methanothermobacter thermautotrophicus) [Harms96a, Sauer98a]. During the catalytic cycle the methyl group is transferred from N5-methyltetrahydromethanopterin to the cob(I)amide prosthetic group, and then from the cobamide to coenzyme M. Only the latter transfer is sodium ion-dependent [Stupperich93, Gartner93, Weiss94, Harms95, Harms96a, Harms97].

It has been proposed that methyl transfer from MtrA to coenzyme M is associated with a conformational change of the protein and that this change drives the electrogenic translocation of the sodium ions [Gottschalk01]. The reaction starts with a methyl group transfer from N5-methyltetrahydromethanopterin (methyl-H4MPT) bound to MtrH to the upper ligation site of Coα-[α-(5-hydroxybenzimidazolyl)]-cob(I)amide, forming Coα-[α-(5-hydroxybenzimidazolyl)]-Coβ-methylcob(III)amide. The methyl group is subsequently transferred to coenzyme M in the presence of sodium ions [Gartner94].
